title: Settlement Note: Miles Driven Beyond the Allowance on a Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
Mileage on a Keyturn Trip Booking is settled once, at the end of the trip, against the allowance standing on the reservation at that moment, including any miles granted by an extension or bought mid-trip.

Miles beyond the allowance are charged at the plan's overage rate, after the plan's grace miles have been taken off the excess; the grace is a deduction from the excess and never a threshold that has to be crossed before any miles are charged.

Where the reservation's unused allowance is zero or positive no overage line is raised at all, and no line is raised where the plan offers unlimited mileage on a vehicle eligible for it.

Where the only odometer readings on file come from the host, the overage is charged on those readings but is capped at the excess the telematics record of the same trip would have produced where one exists; a dispute over the reading is settled on the authoritative reading rather than split between the two.

The overage line is raised only while the reservation is in the completed or settled state, since the miles cannot be known before the vehicle is back.

### The grace as a deduction, worked through

*Hypothetical inputs: a reservation whose unused allowance stands at 40 miles short, on a plan whose grace is 10 miles and whose overage rate is 0.42 USD for each mile.*

The excess is 40 miles. The grace of 10 miles is taken off that excess, leaving 30 chargeable miles. Thirty chargeable miles at 0.42 USD each gives an overage of 12.60 USD.

The grace is subtracted from the excess; it is not a level the excess must pass before any mile becomes chargeable.

*Hypothetical, at the boundary.* Where the unused allowance stands at exactly 10 miles short on that same plan, the grace of 10 miles absorbs the whole excess and the chargeable miles come to nothing; no money is due on the mileage settlement.

### When no line is raised at all

| Situation at the end of the trip | Overage line |
|---|---|
| Unused allowance is positive | None is raised. |
| Unused allowance is exactly zero | None is raised. |
| Unlimited mileage offered by the plan on a vehicle eligible for it | None is raised. |
| Unused allowance is negative | Raised on the excess, less the grace. |

### Readings, and the cap they carry

Where the only odometer readings on file come from the host, the settlement is computed on those readings, but the amount is held down to the excess that the telematics record of the same trip would have produced, where such a record exists. Where the two readings disagree, the settlement follows the authoritative reading whole; it is never split between the two.

### The state gate

The overage line is raised only while the reservation stands in the completed or settled state, read from the reservation's own record — its status and its unused allowance — before the line is raised and correlated by the reservation's reference number. Before the vehicle is back the miles cannot be known, which is what keeps the settlement out of the earlier states.
